newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST-ABS-CBN 6-mths net seen up 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-ABS-CBN 6-mths net seen up 22 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' biggest television firm, ABS-CBN Inc, could post good results next month as it recovers from a row with advertisers, but the fight has left a scar that could haunt the company next year, analysts said on Wednesday.
The broadcaster could post a 22 percent rise in net income to 824 million pesos ($31.3 million) in the first six months ending June, a Reuters poll of seven stock brokerages showed.
Full year 1997 net profit projections yielded an average of 1,803 million pesos, up 17.84 percent from the previous year.
ABS-CBN, born in 1946 as Bolinao Electronics Corp assembling radio equipment from war-surplus parts, dominates the radio and TV industry in this archipelago of 68 million people.
In 1996, it reported a 41 percent audience share in the capital Manila, compared to its closest competitor's 22 percent. In the provinces, it reported a 70 percent audience share.

Its millions of TV viewers, fed on a daily diet of recycled South American soap operas and local tragicomedies, give ABS-CBN such clout that in March it announced a huge 22 percent hike in advertising rates -- and almost succeeded in getting advertisers to pay the full increase.
"They got a 21 percent hike (for prime time). ABS had to give in just a token one percent and they won," ING Barings analyst Giovanni dela Rosa said.
The advertisers had insisted they would never agree to a hike of more than 15 percent and cancelled orders for over a week, shutting the window that brings in 80 percent of ABS's revenue.
The boycott led to a 15 percent drop in the first quarter net to 248 million pesos from 291 million a year ago.
The advertisers eventually gave in and analysts said ABS's full year income would meet the company's target.
Averages from the poll showed ABS could post a 1997 net of 1,803 million pesos, up 17.84 percent from last year.
But getting a rate hike next year could prove tough.
"It will be difficult for ABS to raise rates further. What will really hurt is the perception among advertisers that the rates are too high," said Spencer Yap of BPI Capital Corp.
ABS has already moved to tackle the issue. It is now segmenting its market, hoping to get more revenue from a new channel targeted at the growing number of wealthy Filipinos.
Its new UHF channel, Studio 23, was expected to move beyond start-up phase by 1998 and contribute significantly to growth.
The launch of the new channel is considered by many as yet another example of the marketing savvy of the company, which rebounded after being muzzled by dictator Ferdinand Marcos.

In 1952, Bolinao Electronics Corp changed its name to Alto Broadcasting System (ABS) and five years later it merged with Chronicle Broadcasting Network (CBN) to form ABS-CBN, which came under the control of the powerful Lopez family.
But the family fell out with Malacanang, the presidential palace, and in 1972 the firm's chief, Eugenio Lopez Jr, was arrested on charges of conspiring to assassinate Marcos.
Lopez escaped from prison in 1977 and regained ABS in 1986 after Marcos was ousted.
Proud of its role, the firm marketed itself with new zeal.
